messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autodetect - inference-api (us-west-1) ELB 5xx spike >15% over 5m, p95 latency >1200ms. Auto-sevscore=7. PagerDuty: ops-oncall
ops-oncall: Oncall here, paging SREs. Who's got the surface?
maria_s: TG health is flapping in us-west-1 AZ-A. Targets deregistering then re-registering. Seeing EBS io wait spikes on i-0abc1234 (/dev/nvme1n1) with io timeout in dmesg.
priya_k: Metrics match—EBS read latency aligns with ELB 502/504 spikes. Likely AZ-level EBS backend degradation, or noisy neighbor. Checking ASG health and cross-zone traffic.
tom_h: Preparing cross-region mitigation runbook. Recommend gradual DNS weight shift to inference-api-us-west-2, avoid full cutover to prevent cold-cache storm.
lauren_o: CS: multiple customers reporting batch embedding timeouts. I'm drafting customer-facing blurb. Need ETA for mitigation.
ops-oncall: Mitigation plan: 1) relax TG healthchecks to stop thrash, 2) deregister impacted instances and spin replacements, 3) attempt ASG scale-up in same region, 4) if AZ remains unhealthy, shift weighted Route53 traffic to us-west-2. Executing step 1 now.
incident-bot: Command recorded: aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-infer --health-check-interval-seconds 10 --health-check-timeout-seconds 2 (placeholder)
maria_s: Done — healthcheck intervals relaxed. Deregister thrash dropped immediately.
priya_k: describe-target-health output snippet: ```TargetHealthDescriptions: [{Target:{Id:'i-0abc1234'}, TargetHealth:{State:'unhealthy', Reason:'ELB.Timeout'}}, ...]```
tom_h: Detaching i-0abc1234 from ASG and launching replacement (aws autoscaling detach-instances --instance-ids i-0abc1234 --should-decrement-desired-capacity false).
ops-oncall: Replacement boots good but EBS AZ metrics still high. AWS status shows EBS API errors in that AZ — opening ticket. https://status.aws.amazon.com/ (link placeholder)
lauren_o: Notifying top-10 impacted customers with interim status: "We are investigating storage-related errors in a single AZ and routing traffic to healthy capacity. We'll update shortly." CS copy posted.
maria_s: Initiating partial DNS weight shift: current 100% us-west-1 -> plan 70/30 us-west-1/us-west-2. TTL is 60s.
priya_k: Note on TTLs: 60s gives quick churn, we'll ramp weights over 10 minutes.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident escalated to P1. Next handoff to tom_h in +30m.
ops-oncall: Switching to chat-ops. I'll watch ELB 5xx and latency dashboards. who can watch storage?
eng-runtime: Deploying hotfix to edge-cache to reduce EBS read pressure (short-lived read-through cache).
maria_s: Edge-cache deploy completed. EBS read traffic down ~45%, embedding errors dropping. 5xx down to ~3%.
priya_k: Route53 weight shift to 50/50 completed. TG deregisters stopped. EBS latency still above baseline but trending down.
lauren_o: Customer update posted: "We've mitigated the worst of the errors; we're routing traffic away from the impacted AZ and expect full restoration within 2 hours." CS acknowledged :thumbsup:.
tom_h: AWS case update: escalated to EBS engineering; may require AZ hardware maintenance. They provided a long window. We'll keep weighted routing until they confirm recovery.
ops-oncall: Actions remaining: maintain 50/50 until p95 <300ms for 30m, keep replacement instances, update customers, schedule postmortem. Assigning PM: lauren_o.
incident-bot: Incident timeline created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2461234567 (internal link)
lauren_o: Taking PM ownership. I'll collect timeline, impacts, and coordinate postmortem and any customer credits.
maria_s: Current state: 5xx steady ~1-2%, p95 ~280ms. I'll monitor and plan to restore 100% us-west-1 after 1h of stable metrics.
priya_k: Agreed. Scheduling handoff summary at +1h. Good work team.
ops-oncall: Moving to monitoring state; chat-ops closed. Notes updated in PagerDuty and incident doc.
